claim: CodeVetter can sample CPU inside one isolated capture-scoped owned Node request, retain only contained repository sources above fixed thresholds, and refuse source attribution when the samples do not support it.

observed: A 40 ms repository function produced a material contained source candidate without application source modifications.
An extension-shaped static request did not start a CPU profile.
Two overlapping dynamic requests contaminated the process-wide profile and produced no source candidate.
Generated output, malformed profiles, raw query text, absolute paths, and credential-shaped function text were not exposed.

detector.name: browser_server_cpu_hotspot
detector.reason: Request CPU samples did not cross the fixed repository sample and share thresholds.

real_product.verdict: The 2.26 second development request was approximately 96.2% idle samples and contained no repository self-CPU sample. CodeVetter correctly withheld an optimization candidate instead of blaming the static route owner.

bounds.raw_profiles: owned temporary runtime directory only; removed during cleanup
bounds.source_authority: regular contained file or closed Next server webpack-internal source URL

claim_boundaries: V8 sampling begins immediately before handler dispatch and perturbs the diagnostic request.
Sample counts estimate on-CPU and idle states; they do not assign wall time exclusively to a source line.
Overlapping dynamic requests invalidate source attribution because the V8 profiler is process-wide.
A config-disabled Next development runtime, system Chrome, failed product assertion, and one local machine do not establish production performance.
A source edit still requires compatible paired measurement and project-owned correctness evidence.
